author: Jack J. Burleson

markdown.markdown:
**Research question:** Which of the 16 RVL-CDIP classes drive the remaining misclassification budget, and which confusion pairs account for it?

**Formal write-up:** [`results/confusion-matrices.qmd`](../results/confusion-matrices.html) · [`appendix/misclassifications.qmd`](../appendix/misclassifications.html) · [`reports/monte_carlo/corpus.summary.md`](https://github.com/Exios66/AMFAM_capstone/blob/main/reports/monte_carlo/corpus.summary.md)

---


Three classes are the persistent **over-attractors** and one pair is the hardest discriminator. On the 4,641-row / 1,512-image Monte Carlo corpus, the top off-diagonal confusion pairs are:

| Expected → Predicted | Errors |
|---|---:|
| `letter` → `memo` | 53 |
| `budget` → `invoice` | 52 |
| `invoice` → `form` | 41 |
| `specification` → `form` | 41 |
| `budget` → `form` | 33 |
| `scientific_report` → `form` | 23 |

::: {.callout-warning title="Form is the Dominant Error Sink"}
**`form`** is the dominant error sink: `*` → `form` pairs (`invoice`, `specification`, `budget`, `scientific_report`, `resume`, `questionnaire`) account for the single largest share of the miss budget, driven by filled analytical/QA data sheets and labeled charts/tables whose form-layout footer (fields, approval blocks) pulls check 10 ahead of checks 7/8/9/13.
:::

![Per-class accuracy on the 1,120-image slice](../charts/per_class_accuracy_qwen3.7-flash_v11.8_reasoning_1600_balanced_1120.svg)

**Per-class accuracy on the 1,120-image slice (v11.8):** easiest classes `email`, `resume`, `memo`, `file_folder`, `advertisement` (~90%+); hardest `budget` (~65%), `presentation` (~69%), `scientific_report` (~73%), `letter` (~74%).

::: {.callout-important title="Near-Miss Ceiling"}
Of 195 errors on the 1,120 run, **72 (36.9%) were near-misses** — the runner-up label equals the ground truth. Those are recoverable in principle without new model knowledge, making ~37% of the remaining error budget a **labeling/selection problem** rather than a **perception problem**.
:::

**Conclusion.** Effort should concentrate on (1) the `form` over-attractor (check-10 ordering vs the analytical-content checks), (2) the `budget`↔`invoice` estimate/billing boundary, and (3) `letter`↔`memo` correspondence headers — in that order. Full reasoning traces for all 195 errors (70 pairs) are browsable in the [misclassification appendix](../appendix/misclassifications.html).

::: {.memo-sources}
*Sources:* `reports/monte_carlo/corpus.summary.md` · `reports/misclassification_reasoning_*_1600_balanced_1120.md` · [github.com/Exios66/AMFAM_capstone](https://github.com/Exios66/AMFAM_capstone)
:::

---

## What questions or uncertainties remain?

Per-class difficulty is slice-dependent — the 160 curated slice shows near-perfect per-class scores while 1,120 shows the collapse above. Whether the difficulty ordering (`form`, `budget`/`invoice`, `letter`/`memo`) is stable across production-noise samples is untested; the v3/v4 disjoint slices (96.2% / 79.4% at v16) hint it is only roughly stable.

## What other levers may also fix these classes?

The [few-shot exemplar memo](exemplar-mining.qmd) mines correct traces for exactly these pairs as in-context examples; the [hasty-stop memo](hasty-stop-words.qmd) shows trigger words that cause premature commit before the cascade reaches the discriminating checks.
